content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published consolidated guidelines on the treatment of drug-susceptible tuberculosis (DS-TB) in Module 4 of its tuberculosis guidelines. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of DS-TB, including treatment regimens, care, and monitoring of patients. The guidelines are available in both electronic and print formats, with ISBNs 978-92-4-004812-6 and 978-92-4-004813-3, respectively. The publication is copyrighted by WHO in 2022, and its content can be copied, redistributed, and adapted for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. The guidelines emphasize the treatment of DS-TB using a 6-month regimen consisting of four first-line TB medicines: isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide. This regimen has been widely adopted globally and has a treatment success rate of approximately 85%. The recommendations are based on seminal TB treatment studies conducted by the British Medical Research Council in the mid-20th century. The guidelines also include recommendations for treatment modalities, formulations, administration frequency, and patient care during treatment. The updated guidelines consolidate evidence-based recommendations from the 2010 and 2017 updates and introduce new recommendations for 4-month regimens to treat DS-TB, developed during the 2021 guideline development process. These updates align with the End TB Strategy, which aims to provide treatment and support for all individuals with TB. The guidelines are intended to inform policy decisions by national TB control program managers, policymakers, and medical practitioners in diverse settings. The objectives of the updated guidelines are to provide recommendations based on newly emerged evidence for DS-TB treatment and to summarize changes in the new guidelines alongside existing WHO recommendations. The guidance outlines specific recommendations for treatment management, care, and monitoring of DS-TB patients, developed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) approach. These recommendations are the result of collaborative efforts by experts in public health policy, TB program management, patient care, and affected communities. The guidelines recommend that new patients with pulmonary TB receive a 6-month regimen containing rifampicin (2HRZE/4HR), with daily dosing throughout the course of therapy being the optimal frequency. These recommendations are supported by strong evidence and are intended to maximize treatment efficacy and patient outcomes.
